chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reported to me from his father, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim and al-Fadhl the two Ash'aris, from Abdullah ibn Bukair, from Zurarah, that Abu Ja'far or Abu Abdillah, peace be upon them both, said:
"The closest a servant comes to disbelief is when he befriends a man on the basis of religion, then keeps count of his stumbles and slips in order to fault him with them someday."

key_terms.الكفر: Disbelief (kufr) — the rejection of faith; here used to describe how closely fault-finding approaches the boundary of unbelief
key_terms.زلّات: Slips, errors — closely synonymous with عثرات, emphasizing the unintentional nature of human failings
key_terms.عثرات: Stumbles, lapses — referring to minor faults and mistakes that every person inevitably commits
key_terms.يواخي: To befriend, to establish brotherhood — from the root أخ (brother), referring to the Islamic practice of forming bonds of religious brotherhood

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about befriending someone to find their faults?
ai.summary: This hadith delivers a stern ethical warning against the hypocrisy of befriending someone under the guise of religious brotherhood only to secretly catalog their faults for later use. The Imam draws a direct connection between this behavior and disbelief (kufr), indicating that such deceptive surveillance of a fellow believer's shortcomings is among the gravest spiritual dangers. In the early Shia community, where bonds of religious brotherhood were essential for survival and solidarity, betraying that trust through fault-finding was considered a fundamental violation of faith itself.

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 6. He said: Abul Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan reorted to me from his father, who reported from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, who reported from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, who reported from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibrahim and al-Fadhl - the two Ash’aries - from Abdullah ibn Bukair, from Zurarah who reported that Abu Ja’far or Abu Abdillah (as) said:

"When a servant of Allah befriends someone, under the pretense of religion, with a motive to find out his drawbacks and errors, so that he would then taunt that man, he draws himself closest to becoming an infidel."
